  1. com.sbancuz.offscreen.api

Animate windows, elements and custom captions

To animate a window or control, choose the properties to change, describe their changes in a timeline and play that timeline. You can also supply your own caption font or draw through a rendering callback.

Choose what to animate

A timeline is a set of instructions. Building it does not start an animation. The object you play it on decides which properties are available and what their coordinates mean.

Animation targets
TargetPropertiesCoordinates
Desktop windowPosition, size, opacity and content tintPosition is on the desktop; width and height use logical window coordinates.
Built-in widgetPosition, size, opacity and tintPosition and size use GUI units relative to the widget’s parent.
Animated elementThe above properties, plus rotation and scalePosition and size use GUI units; rotation uses degrees. Draw its contents in local coordinates starting at zero.

To rotate an icon or a group of controls, use an animated element. The operating system’s native window border cannot rotate. Channel.EFFECT_PROGRESS is a number your own effect can read; changing it has no visible effect until your renderer uses it.

Timing and ownership

Create timelines with the calls below. Durations use real seconds from a clock that only moves forward; they are not frame counts. Timeline values can be built in common code, but playing a window animation, handling its completion and touching graphics must happen on Minecraft’s client thread.

Build a timeline
CallArgumentsBehavior
Timeline.to(channel, end, seconds, easing)Property, destination, duration and curveRead the starting value when the clip begins, then move toward the destination.
Timeline.fromTo(channel, start, end, seconds, easing)Property, explicit start and end, duration and curveSet the chosen start value first. Useful when an entrance must begin invisible.
Timeline.waitFor(seconds)Delay in secondsPause this sequence before its next step, without changing a property.
first.then(next)The next timelineRun one step after another.
Timeline.parallel(clips...)Timelines using separate propertiesRun the clips together. ZenScript uses with for this kind of composition.
timeline.repeat(count)A finite count from 1 to 16384Repeat the instructions with fresh starting values each time. The expanded timeline must also fit the size limit.

The easing curve controls how quickly the value changes within a clip. Choose Easing.SINE.inOut() for a smooth start and finish, in() for a slow start, or out() for a slow finish. Other families include Linear, Quad, Cubic, Quart, Quint, Expo, Circ, Back, Elastic and Bounce. Back, Elastic and Bounce can add overshoot or bouncing.

Use Easing.curve("exponential", "ease-out") to choose a curve by name, or supply a DoubleUnaryOperator for your own curve. ZenScript supplies custom curves through Animations.curve. Return finite numbers from custom curves; an invalid sample fails the track.

Present, expand and dock an inspector

Once the window has drawn its first frame, call window.animations().play(name, timeline). The name identifies a track in this window. Starting another track with the same name replaces it. Tracks with different names still replace one another if they try to change the same property.

Position, size and appearance helpers
CallArgumentsResult
Motions.moveTo(x, y, seconds, easing)Desktop destination, duration and curveMove the window to that position.
Motions.resizeTo(width, height, seconds, easing)Logical window dimensions, duration and curveResize the window; its screen is laid out again as its size changes.
Motions.fadeTo(opacity, seconds, easing)Opacity from 0 to 1, duration and curveFade toward the requested opacity.
Motions.colorTo(rgb, seconds, easing)Packed RGB tint, duration and curveTint the window content. White leaves its original colors visible.
window.displayBounds()No argumentsRead the display rectangle used to calculate the positions in the recipe.

The recipe below reveals an inspector, expands it, waits, docks it at the side and returns it to the center. Each parallel group changes different properties. The waits provide reading time between moves.

Keep the returned Animator.Playback handle to control that run:

Playback controls
CallBehavior
pause()Stop progression. Paused time is not added to the animation when it resumes.
resume()Continue a paused run from its current position.
cancel() / close()Stop future steps and release resources owned by the run. The current visual values stay where they are; cancellation does not move the window back.
whenFinished(callback)Receive this playback once it finishes, is cancelled or fails. A callback added after completion runs immediately.
failure() / observerFailures()Read a track failure or errors thrown by its completion callbacks.

For an entrance that must take effect before the window is shown, use OffscreenAPI.openAnimated for a local screen or OffscreenSimpleFactory.openAnimated for a server panel. These apply the entrance’s starting state before showing the new window. On a synchronized open, the entrance may animate the waiting screen; use isReady to check whether the server panel has arrived.

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.animation.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;

final class ChoreographyRecipe {
    static Animator.Playback run(Window window) {
        var area = window.displayBounds();
        var reveal = Timeline.parallel(
            Motions.moveTo(area.x() + area.width() * 0.24,
                area.y() + area.height() * 0.2,
                0.45,
                Easing.QUINT.inOut()),
            Motions.resizeTo(area.width() * 0.52,
                area.height() * 0.52,
                0.45,
                Easing.QUINT.inOut()),
            Motions.colorTo(0xFFFFFF, 0.45, Easing.SINE.inOut()),
            Timeline.fromTo(Channel.OPACITY, 0, 1, 0.45, Easing.SINE.inOut()));
        var expand = Timeline.parallel(
            Motions.moveTo(area.x() + area.width() * 0.12,
                area.y() + area.height() * 0.1,
                0.65,
                Easing.QUINT.inOut()),
            Motions.resizeTo(area.width() * 0.76,
                area.height() * 0.76,
                0.65,
                Easing.QUINT.inOut()),
            Motions.colorTo(0xFFFFFF, 0.65, Easing.SINE.inOut()),
            Motions.fadeTo(1, 0.65, Easing.SINE.inOut()));
        var dock = Timeline.parallel(
            Motions.moveTo(area.x() + area.width() * 0.66,
                area.y() + area.height() * 0.16,
                0.55,
                Easing.QUINT.inOut()),
            Motions.resizeTo(area.width() * 0.3,
                area.height() * 0.64,
                0.55,
                Easing.QUINT.inOut()),
            Motions.colorTo(0xC8DCFF, 0.55, Easing.SINE.inOut()),
            Motions.fadeTo(0.9, 0.55, Easing.SINE.inOut()));
        var restore = Timeline.parallel(
            Motions.moveTo(area.x() + area.width() * 0.24,
                area.y() + area.height() * 0.2,
                0.7,
                Easing.QUINT.inOut()),
            Motions.resizeTo(area.width() * 0.52,
                area.height() * 0.52,
                0.7,
                Easing.QUINT.inOut()),
            Motions.colorTo(0xFFFFFF, 0.7, Easing.SINE.inOut()),
            Motions.fadeTo(1, 0.7, Easing.SINE.inOut()));
        var presentation = reveal
            .then(expand)
            .then(Timeline.waitFor(1.2))
            .then(dock)
            .then(Timeline.waitFor(2.5))
            .then(restore);
    window.exitAnimation(Motions.fadeTo(0, .3, Easing.SINE.in()));
        return window.animations()
            .play("inspector",
            presentation)
            .whenFinished(result -> {
            if (result.failure() != null) result.failure().printStackTrace();
        });
    }
    // Client action: cancellation keeps current geometry; it is not a rollback.
    static void stop(Animator.Playback handle) {
        handle.cancel();
    }
}

#side client
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Animations;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Window;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.AnimationHandle;

function presentInspector(window as Window) as AnimationHandle {
    val area = window.displayBounds();
    val reveal = Animations.move(area.x + area.width * 0.24,
        area.y + area.height * 0.2,
        0.45,
        Animations.ease("quint",
        "inOut"))
        .with(Animations.size(area.width * 0.52,
            area.height * 0.52,
            0.45,
            Animations.ease("quint",
            "inOut")))
        .with(Animations.color(0xFFFFFF, 0.45, Animations.ease("sine", "inOut")))
        .with(Animations.set(Animations.property("opacity"),
            0)
        .then(Animations.fade(1,
            0.45,
            Animations.ease("sine",
            "inOut"))));
    val expand = Animations.move(area.x + area.width * 0.12,
        area.y + area.height * 0.1,
        0.65,
        Animations.ease("quint",
        "inOut"))
        .with(Animations.size(area.width * 0.76,
            area.height * 0.76,
            0.65,
            Animations.ease("quint",
            "inOut")))
        .with(Animations.color(0xFFFFFF, 0.65, Animations.ease("sine", "inOut")))
        .with(Animations.fade(1, 0.65, Animations.ease("sine", "inOut")));
    val dock = Animations.move(area.x + area.width * 0.66,
        area.y + area.height * 0.16,
        0.55,
        Animations.ease("quint",
        "inOut"))
        .with(Animations.size(area.width * 0.3,
            area.height * 0.64,
            0.55,
            Animations.ease("quint",
            "inOut")))
        .with(Animations.color(0xC8DCFF, 0.55, Animations.ease("sine", "inOut")))
        .with(Animations.fade(0.9, 0.55, Animations.ease("sine", "inOut")));
    val restore = Animations.move(area.x + area.width * 0.24,
        area.y + area.height * 0.2,
        0.7,
        Animations.ease("quint",
        "inOut"))
        .with(Animations.size(area.width * 0.52,
            area.height * 0.52,
            0.7,
            Animations.ease("quint",
            "inOut")))
        .with(Animations.color(0xFFFFFF, 0.7, Animations.ease("sine", "inOut")))
        .with(Animations.fade(1, 0.7, Animations.ease("sine", "inOut")));
    val presentation = reveal
        .then(expand)
        .then(Animations.delay(1.2))
        .then(dock)
        .then(Animations.delay(2.5))
        .then(restore);
    window.exitAnimation(Animations.fade(0, 0.3, Animations.ease("sine", "in")));
    return window.animate("inspector", presentation).whenFinished(function(result) {
        if (result.error != "") print(result.error);
    });
}
function stopPresentation(handle as AnimationHandle) {
    handle.cancel();
}

Animate each element independently

Call window.element(x, y, width, height) for a label, icon or group of drawing commands that needs its own movement. Store the returned AnimatedElement in the screen controller. Creating it does not make it draw itself.

Element calls
CallArgumentsUse
element(x, y, width, height)GUI position and positive sizeCreate the region whose contents will move together.
element.animations().play(name, timeline)Track name and timelineAnimate this element independently of the desktop window.
element.render(mouseX, mouseY, partialTicks, draw)Pointer position, frame timing and drawing callbackDraw from the screen’s render callback. Draw inside the element using local coordinates.
element.contains(mouseX, mouseY)Pointer position in the parent’s coordinatesCheck whether the pointer hits the visible element after its movement, rotation and scale.
element.localPoint(mouseX, mouseY)Pointer position in the parent’s coordinatesConvert the pointer to element-local coordinates for a control inside the region.
element.close()No argumentsRelease the element when the screen is disposed.

Forward input to your own controls after the hit check; an animated element does not create buttons or dispatch clicks for you. A fully transparent element does not receive a hit. The window releases its owned elements when it closes, but closing an element at screen disposal also handles navigation that removes the screen while keeping the window open.

Built-in widgets already expose their own animations() controller; ZenScript calls it animate. Their hit regions follow their animated position and size, so they do not need a separate element just to move.

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.animation.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.AnimatedElement;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;
import net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui;

final class ElementRecipe {
    private final AnimatedElement label;
    ElementRecipe(Window window) {
        label = window.element(20, 30, 100, 24);
        label.animations()
            .play("spin",
            Timeline.to(Channel.ROTATION,
            360,
            2,
            Easing.SINE.inOut()));
        label.animations()
            .play("pulse",
            Motions.oscillate(Channel.SCALE_X,
            1,
            .1,
            2,
            2));
    }
    // Render callback: local coordinates start at zero inside this layer.
    void draw(int mouseX, int mouseY, float partial) {
        label.render(mouseX, mouseY, partial, canvas -> {
            Gui.drawRect(0, 0, (int) canvas.width(), (int) canvas.height(), 0xFF8050C0);
        });
    }
    boolean hit(int mouseX, int mouseY) {
        return label.contains(mouseX, mouseY);
    }
    void dispose() {
        label.close();
    }
}

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.animation.*
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window
import net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui

class ElementKotlin(window: Window) {
    private val label = window.element(20.0, 30.0, 100.0, 24.0)
    init {
        label.animations()
            .play("spin",
            Timeline.to(Channel.ROTATION,
            360.0,
            2.0,
            Easing.SINE.inOut()))
        label.animations()
            .play("pulse",
            Motions.oscillate(Channel.SCALE_X,
            1.0,
            .1,
            2.0,
            2.0))
    }
    fun draw(x: Int, y: Int, partial: Float) {
        label.render(x.toDouble(), y.toDouble(), partial) { canvas ->
            Gui.drawRect(0,
                0,
                canvas.width()
                .toInt(),
                canvas.height()
                .toInt(),
                0xFF8050C0.toInt())
        }
    }
    fun hit(x: Int, y: Int) = label.contains(x.toDouble(), y.toDouble())
    fun dispose() { label.close() }
}

#side client
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Animations;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Window;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.AnimatedElement;

function createLayer(window as Window) as AnimatedElement {
    val label = window.element(20, 30, 100, 24);
    label.animate("spin", Animations.to(Animations.property("rotation"), 360, 2,
        Animations.ease("sine", "inOut")));
    label.animate("pulse",
        Animations.oscillate(Animations.property("scale_x"),
        1,
        0.1,
        2,
        2));
    return label;
}
// Call from the screen's draw callback with its current pointer coordinates.
function drawLayer(label as AnimatedElement, x as int, y as int, partial as float) {
    label.draw(x, y, partial, function(canvas) {
        canvas.rect(0, 0, canvas.width as int, canvas.height as int, 0xFF8050C0);
    });
}
function hitLayer(label as AnimatedElement, x as int, y as int) as bool {
    return label.contains(x, y);
}
function disposeLayer(label as AnimatedElement) {
    label.close();
}

Use a formatted font for the title and controls

To draw the title and window controls with your own font, first open the window with a custom title bar. Then call window.captionRenderer(renderer) and keep the returned CaptionHandle. This changes the custom bar’s text; the operating system’s taskbar title remains plain.

Caption setup
CallArgumentsUse
window.captionTitle(text)Full title string, including your font’s formatting codesSet the title displayed by the custom bar.
window.captionLabels(minimize, middle, close)The three control labelsChoose the glyphs drawn for the window controls.
CaptionRenderer.of(measure, height, draw)Width function, height function and drawing functionConnect a font provider to the custom bar.
window.captionRenderer(renderer)Your completed rendererInstall it and receive the handle used to remove it.

The measuring function returns the width of the supplied text, and the height function returns the font height. The draw callback receives a role, the unchanged text, its position and a base color. Use the role to tell title text from a control label when your font needs different treatment.

Use the same formatting rules for measuring and drawing. Otherwise the bar may reserve the wrong amount of space or clip a label. If your provider chooses its own text colors, keep them readable against the configured bar tint; a transparent bar cannot know the desktop colors behind it.

The code borrows Minecraft’s font renderer. Replace all three functions together when using another provider, and close only the returned caption handle during teardown. Do not close a global font renderer borrowed from Minecraft or another mod.

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.CaptionHandle;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.CaptionRenderer;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;

final class CaptionRecipe {
    static CaptionHandle install(Window window) {
        window.captionTitle("§bTools §f— §dPreview");
        window.captionLabels("_", "□", "×");
        return window.captionRenderer(CaptionRenderer.of(
                text -> Minecraft.getMinecraft().fontRenderer.getStringWidth(text),
                () -> Minecraft.getMinecraft().fontRenderer.FONT_HEIGHT,
                (role, text, x, y, baseColor) -> {
                    Minecraft.getMinecraft().fontRenderer.drawString(text,
                        x,
                        y,
                        baseColor);
                }));
    }
    // Teardown: removes only this contribution, even after a newer font replaced it.
    static void remove(CaptionHandle handle) {
        handle.close();
    }
}

import mods.offscreencleanroom.Windows;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Window;

function installCaption(window as Window) as CaptionHandle {

Attach a shader or in-game renderer

To run your own renderer at a chosen point, call window.renderAttachments().add(stage, draw, cleanup). Pass the rendering stage, a drawing callback and a cleanup function for resources your renderer owns. Keep the returned receipt if you may remove the renderer before its window closes.

Choose a rendering stage
StageWhere it drawsAvailable setup
BACKGROUNDInside the desktop window, before its screen contentThe window’s drawing area has been cleared.
FOREGROUNDInside the desktop window, after the content and captionWindow postprocessing has not run yet.
WORLDIn Minecraft’s worldThe current camera and world projection are active.
HUDOver Minecraft’s game viewThe game’s GUI projection is active.

The callback receives a RenderAttachments.Context for this draw only. A nonzero texture() value gives access to the supplied texture during that callback. Do not store the context or texture ID for use in a later frame; both are borrowed from the current draw.

Offscreen supplies the place to draw, not the shader or effect. Your addon creates its shader programs and other graphics resources and releases them in the cleanup callback. For an effect driven by animation, read window.animationValue(Channel.EFFECT_PROGRESS) from your renderer. This value remains available during a frozen exit.

All render callbacks and their cleanup run on the client thread. Close the receipt when the attachment is no longer needed; closing the owning window also removes attachments. Removing an old receipt affects only its own registration.

import java.util.function.Consumer;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.RenderAttachments;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;

final class RenderHookRecipe {
    static RenderAttachments.Receipt attach(Window window,
            Consumer<RenderAttachments.Context> addonDraw, Runnable addonCleanup) {
        return window.renderAttachments().add(RenderAttachments.Stage.WORLD, frame -> {
            if (frame.texture() != 0) addonDraw.accept(frame);
        }, addonCleanup);
    }
    static void remove(RenderAttachments.Receipt handle) {
        handle.close();
    }
}

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.RenderAttachments
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window

object RenderHookKotlin {
    fun attach(window: Window, addonDraw: (RenderAttachments.Context) -> Unit,
               addonCleanup: () -> Unit): RenderAttachments.Receipt =
        window.renderAttachments().add(RenderAttachments.Stage.WORLD, { frame ->
            if (frame.texture() != 0) addonDraw(frame)
        }, addonCleanup)
    fun remove(handle: RenderAttachments.Receipt) { handle.close() }
}

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.RenderAttachments
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window

object RenderHookScala:
  def attach(window: Window, addonDraw: RenderAttachments#Context => Unit,
             addonCleanup: () => Unit): RenderAttachments#Receipt =
    window.renderAttachments().add(RenderAttachments.Stage.WORLD, frame => {

    }, () => addonCleanup())
  def remove(handle: RenderAttachments#Receipt): Unit = handle.close()

#side client
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Window;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.RenderAction;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.RenderHandle;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Action;

function attachRenderer(window as Window, addonDraw as RenderAction,
        addonCleanup as Action) as RenderHandle {
    return window.render("world", function(frame) {
        if (frame.texture != 0) addonDraw.draw(frame);
    }, addonCleanup);
}
function removeRenderer(handle as RenderHandle) {
    handle.close();
}

Failure, reload and closing

Each retained handle has one job. Release it when that part of the screen is finished:

Cleanup and failure behavior
Handle or resourceHow to finishIf a callback fails
Playbackcancel() or close()The track stops. Inspect failure() for the cause and observerFailures() for errors in completion callbacks.
Animated elementclose() from screen disposalDo not keep forwarding drawing or input after disposal.
Caption handleclose()The caption falls back to Minecraft’s font; the handle retains the failure.
Render attachment receiptclose()The failing attachment removes itself and attempts its cleanup without removing other attachments.
WindowOffscreenAPI.close(window)Its session and remaining owned visual resources are released through the window lifecycle.

An exit animation is set with window.exitAnimation(timeline). When you close that window, server interaction ends first and the finite exit plays using a frozen image of the screen. During the exit, isOpen stays true, isReady is false and the status is CLOSING. The frozen image is visual feedback, not a live inventory.

Use OffscreenAPI.closeImmediately(window) when failed setup or script unload must skip that visual exit. Groovy-owned window cleanup already uses immediate closure so callbacks from an unloaded script cannot continue running.

For resources created by an animation action, use that action context’s own helper so the run can release them. Visual trails hold snapshots, not copied server containers. They cannot take focus, are limited to 32 per source and close when their animation or source releases them.
